full_judgment:
8. Learned appellate Judge in recording reversal rendered decision that the plaintiff-appellant stated that amicably Hasen got the suit-land whose heirs were Neoti Bibi, Rabeya and Jahuruddin from whom he purchased the suit land by three registered deeds dated 30.11.1981 Exhibit-1 series followed by a Bainapatra dated 15.2.1967 but the said Bainapatra has not been produce before this court. Learned appellate judge found contradictions in the testimonies of P.W.1, 2 and P.W.4 on the execution of Bainapatra and the passing of Baina money of Taka 9,800/- and took the view that simple contradictions of the testimony of P.W.4 was not sufficient to turn down plaintiff's claim in as much as P.Ws.1, 2 and 4 stated that rest amount of Taka 7,200/- was paid at the time of registration of deeds. Learned appellate Judge on a consideration of evidences and facts held that vendors of plaintiff were heirs of Hasen Ali and the deeds, Exhibit-1 series of the plaintiff were genuine and the plaintiff got title to the suit land. Learned appellate Judge took into account the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 217 enunciating proposition that Rent Receipts though not documents of title, are important piece of evidence and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows title and found that said ruling would be relevant if the defendant-respondent could have produced Dhakilas of the Ex-land-lord in the name of Banuram Muchi and held that the learned Munsif misconceived the law. Learned appellate Judge found that in the absence of any document showing that plaintiff was a monthly tenant under defendant it could not be considered at all that the plaintiff was a monthly tenant under defendant. Learned appellate Judge also took the view that Record of Right is simply a presumption of possession and the plaintiff having being in possession of the suit property, he was entitled to get the decree. Learned appellate Judge on a consideration of the evidences of D.W.2 disbelieved the story of dispossession set up by the defendant. Learned appellate Judge totally ignored the story of waqf and found that the same was an insurance of the suit land in the premium of religion. 

 12. Learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner assails the decisions recorded by the learned appellate Judge raising the contention that the learned appellate judge being the last and final judge of fact did not advert to the decisions and reasons reached by learned trial Judge and the judgment under challenge in the civil revision petition having not been a proper judgment of reversal and having contravened the provision contained in Rule 31 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the same cannot be sustained in law. 

 13. Repelling the said contention it is contended on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite parry that learned appellate Judge adverted to the decisions rendered the learned trial Judge rendering decisions on every point involved and the impugned judgment having been a proper judgment of reversal does not warrant any interference by this Court in the exercise of civil revisional jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 14. In the wake of rival contentions advanced from both the sides the fundamental questions that survive for determination this civil revision petition are whether the plaintiff could successfully substantiate his case by legal evidence for being graced with a decree in his favour and whether the judgment under challenge can he characterized as a proper judgment of reversal and whether the grounds canvassed by learned appellate Judge in declaring plaintiff's title on suit property on reversing decision rendered by trial Judge can be sustained or not. 

 15. In approaching the said fundamental question a bird's view of mandate of law enshrined in Order 41, Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be conveniently noticed. Legislature had entrusted a very important duty on the First Appellate Court and was for that court to decide finally all questions of on which disposal of suit would depend. In case of reversal of a trial court's judgment it is incumbent upon lower appellate court to consider evidences and reasoning of the trial court and only, thereafter, to give its reasons for not agreeing with findings of trial court and appellate Judgment reversing the judgment of trial court is required to be adequate and satisfactory and it must contain definite findings on the question involved and must give reasons for reversing decisions recorded by trial court. While differing with trial court on a question of fact the appellate court must remember that the lower court has had the advantage of seeing the demeanour of witnesses and, therefore views regarding their veracity should not be rightly set aside. Lower appellate Court is required to advert to the findings and decisions on which trial court judgment rested. This Rule is imperative and a judgment of reversal which is not in accordance with it, is not one according to law. 

 32. In view of the above discussion conclusion which can be legitimately drawn is that court of appeal though was required to reverse the material findings reached by trial court with reference to evidence on record, the former did not reverse those findings and consequently it is to be held that the judgment of lower appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal and the same suffers from manifest illegality and flagrant error of law and as such cannot be sustained in law.
